The story is written in a very literal, understated, and realistic style. Rather than using figurative language like metaphors, idioms, or literary allusions to convey meaning, the author relies on concrete sensory details (the smell of floor wax, the crescent-shaped burn mark, the jars of pears) and a central plot mystery (the wound-up clock) to build atmosphere and emotional resonance. The few comparisons made in the text are literal-minded similes (e.g., nodding "as if it were about a delivery date") rather than sophisticated metaphors.
